# Pi skill palette blanking — what it is, what it costs, and the contained fix

<Callout tone="decision">
  **This document is the gate before any implementation.** It explains a real, live-reproduced bug,
  resolves the one factual conflict between the two investigation threads, and presents a prototype
  fix that has been watched working end-to-end. Six decisions follow, each with a recommendation and
  its tradeoff. **Silence on an item means the recommendation ships as stated.** Nothing has been
  committed to main; the prototype sits on the scratch branch `scratch/pi-palette-guard-prototype`.
</Callout>

## What you see

You press `$` in the composer to run a skill — or `/` for a provider command — and the menu that
listed your 25 skills a moment ago says, with total confidence:

> **SKILLS — No skills found. Try / to browse provider commands.**

Both halves of that sentence are false. Your skills are still on disk, untouched; and the `/` menu
it recommends was emptied by the same event, because both lists come from the same RPC result. If
the palette is open at the moment the bad publish lands, it collapses in front of you with no user
action. It recovers by itself up to ~2 minutes later (the refresh interval) — unless the cause is
environmental, in which case it stays empty until a server restart or a Settings → providers
refresh.

Both screenshots are from a live dev instance of this worktree (dev-verify recipe), with a scratch
fault making every second enrichment's `get_commands` call fail — the exact shape of the bug, made
observable on demand.

## What it silently costs

The blank menu is the visible symptom. The expensive symptom is invisible: **while the palette is
empty, `$skill` tokens stop expanding on send.** Both send paths expand `$name` →
`/skill:name` against the provider snapshot's skill list (`expandSkillTokensToPromptText` in
`packages/shared/src/composerInlineTokens.ts`, called from `ChatView.tsx`); with an empty list the
text is returned verbatim. We reproduced it live, typing the same message during a blank window and
a healthy one:

<Columns>
  <Column label="During a blank window — literal text sent">
    <HtmlBlock
      height={235}
      html={
        '<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Transcript showing literal $pr-review sent" style="width:100%;display:block">'
      }
    />
  </Column>
  <Column label="Healthy (with the fix, during an injected failure) — expanded">
    <HtmlBlock
      height={235}
      html={
        '<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Transcript showing /skill:pr-review sent" style="width:100%;display:block">'
      }
    />
  </Column>
</Columns>

On the wire (the pi provider log records exactly what the model received):

<Code
  language="text"
  caption="Broken: pi received the literal token — the skill never loaded"
  wrap
  code={
    '"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"$pr-review please review my latest change"}]'
  }
/>

<Code
  language="text"
  caption="Correct: pi expanded the skill and injected its full content into the prompt"
  wrap
  code={
    '"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<skill name=\\"pr-review\\" location=\\"/home/Carl/pi-fathom/plugins/pi-fathom/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md\\" ...>"}]'
  }
/>

Three details make this the centrepiece:

1. **Nothing tells the user.** The agent just proceeds without the skill. In our live run the model
   happened to notice the `$pr-review` hint and read the skill file by itself — a lucky,
   model-dependent save. The designed mechanism did not run, and a subtler skill (a convention, a
   guard-rail, a template) is simply absent with no error anywhere.
2. **The transcript heals itself.** Once the palette recovers, the transcript re-renders the literal
   `$pr-review` as a normal skill chip. Looking back, the conversation is indistinguishable from a
   correct send.
3. **It is easy to hit by accident.** During our verification we deliberately waited for a healthy
   window to capture the "correct" contrast — and still got corrupted, because a bad pass landed in
   the seconds between checking and pressing Enter.

## How often — measured, inferred, unknown

Honesty requires splitting this three ways. **We could not establish a real-world frequency for the
originally-suspected failure, and the measurement says that suspicion was aimed at the wrong
route.**

<Table
  columns={["Claim", "Status", "Evidence"]}
  rows={[
    [
      "`get_commands` is not flaky: p50 1–3 ms, max 67 ms under 24-way load, vs a 90 s timeout",
      "**Measured**",
      "164 real invocations, 0 failures, 0 empty results (sibling thread's harness, real binary)",
    ],
    [
      "Loud enrichment failures are rare: 2 warnings in 62 days (~44,600 passes), both total failures with identified causes",
      "**Measured**",
      "Production journal, Jun 4 – Aug 5",
    ],
    [
      "Every server restart blanks every user's palette until the first enrichment lands (3.4 s idle, ~12 s under load)",
      "**Measured**",
      "Reproduced here (timeline below); 55 restarts in the 62-day journal window",
    ],
    [
      "A *successful* `get_commands` returning an empty list blanks the palette persistently and silently",
      "**Reproduced**",
      "Sibling thread pointed pi at a different agent dir: success, 0 skills, no diagnostic",
    ],
    [
      "A transient `get_commands`-only rejection (the original hypothesis) happens at some real-world rate",
      "**Unknown — and implausible**",
      "It requires the pi child to die inside the 1–67 ms between the two calls, after 3.4–12 s of successful work",
    ],
    [
      "The rate of silent empty publishes in production",
      "**Unknowable today**",
      "The failure path logs nothing: `.catch(() => undefined)`, then an unlogged publish",
    ],
  ]}
/>

The last row is the finding to sit with: **we cannot tell you how often this happens, because the
code is built so that it cannot be counted.** The one failure class that is loud (both RPC calls
failing) is also the safe one — it publishes nothing and the old palette survives. The damaging
class (commands failing or coming back empty while models succeed) is the silent one.

## Does a restart blank the palette? — settled

The two investigation threads disagreed here, and it decides the headline. The code-reading thread
found that the on-disk provider-status cache rehydrates `skills`/`slashCommands` verbatim at boot,
suggesting a restart shows the last known palette. The empirical thread inferred every restart
blanks it. **We settled it by restarting a dev instance and watching the cache file: the restart
blanks the palette — and destroys the cached palette in the process.**

<Code
  language="text"
  caption="On-disk cache (caches/pi.json) across a server restart, polled at 200 ms"
  code={
    '10:07:35.257  skills=25   (healthy cache, server down)\n              -- server start --\n10:07:38.422  skills=0    <- driver\'s placeholder snapshot overwrites the\n                             rehydrated cache and is PERSISTED, ~1.5 s before\n                             the server even finishes listening\n10:07:57.1    "Listening on http://127.0.0.1:13955"\n10:07:58.779  skills=25   <- first successful enrichment lands\n'
  }
/>

Both threads were right about their halves. The cache **is** rehydrated verbatim — and then, within
milliseconds and before the server accepts its first connection, the pi driver's placeholder
snapshot (which carries no commands) is synced over it and **persisted back to disk**. The cached
palette never survives a boot long enough for anyone to see it. What the user sees after every
deploy or restart:

<HtmlBlock
  height={250}
  html={
    '<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Palette blank after restart despite healthy cache" style="width:100%;display:block">'
  }
/>

That screenshot was taken with a scratch 40-second delay on enrichment purely to make the window
photographable; the real window is **3.4–12 s on every restart** (55 restarts in 62 days), and up to
a full **2 minutes** if the first enrichment fails — which is exactly what the production log shows
happened on Jul 20, when `pi` was unresolvable on the unit's PATH straight after a deploy.

One consequence worth naming: because the boot re-persists the placeholder, a blank palette
**inherits across restarts** by design today, and the fix below — which stops blanks reaching the
cache from _enrichment_ — does not close the boot-time clobber (decision D4).

## The fix, prototyped and watched working

The converged shape from both threads, implemented and validated in this worktree: in
`enrichPiSnapshot` (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/PiDriver.ts`), treat a failed **or empty**
commands result as non-authoritative and simply **omit** `slashCommands`/`skills` (and an empty
`models` catalogue) from the published object. The snapshot being enriched is already the
post-carry-forward base, so the previous palette stands with no plumbing changes. The same function
already guards `modelContextWindows` on `models.length > 0` — this is the identical idea applied to
the palette. And the previously-silent path now logs a warning, without which no fix can ever be
verified in production.

## What the fix deliberately does not cover

- **The restart window (D4).** The boot-time placeholder clobber is a different code path
  (`ProviderRegistry` boot sync, not enrichment). The guard stops enrichment blanks from _reaching_
  the cache, which makes restarts inherit the last good palette once the boot clobber is also fixed
  — but on its own, every restart still opens blank for 3.4–12 s.
- **Partial degradation.** pi loading _some_ skills and silently eating the rest (its discovery
  wraps the whole walk in `try { … } catch {}`) still publishes a truncated palette that looks
  authoritative. Only a diagnostics channel out of pi could catch that; out of scope.
- **Enrichment starvation (D5).** Worst-case enrichment (cold boot + two 90 s timeouts) exceeds the
  2-minute refresh interval, so under sustained load the enrichment fiber can be interrupted forever.
  The guard makes that failure invisible (last good palette stands) instead of destructive — the
  right outcome — but the interval/timeout mismatch remains.
- **User-facing signal (D6).** Even with the fix, a genuinely stale palette shows no indicator.
  The composer's empty state still asserts "No skills found" as fact and recommends the `/` menu
  that the same failure empties.

<Card id="d1" heading="D1 · Ship the guard as prototyped" tone="success" badge="VALIDATED" meta={["PiDriver.ts", "~20 lines", "no contract changes"]}>
  The diff above, as-is: a failed `get_commands` no longer overwrites a good palette with an empty
  one. Watched working under fault injection; before/after evidence embedded above. Cost: none
  identified — the publish is otherwise identical, and the registry's existing model-retention
  behaviour is unchanged (the `models` guard merely stops relying on it as a side effect).

  <ReviewChoice itemId="d1" label="D1 — ship the guard" />
</Card>

<Card id="d2" heading="D2 · Treat empty as non-authoritative, not just failure" tone="info" badge="TRADEOFF" meta={["included in prototype", "same tradeoff as PR #172"]}>
  pi's skill discovery swallows filesystem errors at boot and faithfully reports whatever survived,
  so `success` with zero commands is byte-identical to "the user genuinely has no skills". Guarding
  only on rejection leaves that class wide open — and the sibling thread showed it is the *more*
  plausible route to a blank palette. The guard is on the raw commands list, not per-field, so a
  user with prompt templates but no skills still sees a correct (empty) skills section.

**Cost:** a user who genuinely deletes all their skills keeps seeing the stale palette until a
server restart or a Settings → providers refresh. This is exactly the tradeoff the shipped
carry-forward (PR #172) already accepted and documented for base-authoritative providers.

  <ReviewChoice itemId="d2" label="D2 — guard on empty too" />
</Card>

<Card id="d3" heading="D3 · Keep the logWarning on the non-authoritative path" tone="success" badge="OBSERVABILITY" meta={["included in prototype", "1 log line per bad pass"]}>
  62 days of production logs contain zero evidence of the silent class — not because it never
  happened, but because nothing could record it. One warning line (with the cause: rejection vs
  empty result) is what makes the fix verifiable and this failure class countable. At the 2-minute
  cadence a persistent environmental fault would log ~720 lines/day; acceptable for a warning that
  indicates real breakage, and D5 reduces it.

  <ReviewChoice itemId="d3" label="D3 — keep the warning" />
</Card>

<Card id="d4" heading="D4 · The restart window — separate follow-up" tone="warning" badge="NOT COVERED BY D1" meta={["ProviderRegistry boot sync", "55 restarts / 62 days"]}>
  Settled above: every restart blanks every user's palette for 3.4–12 s (2 minutes if the first
  enrichment fails), because the driver's no-commands placeholder overwrites the rehydrated cache
  before the first connection and is persisted back to disk. Two candidate shapes, both outside the
  prototype: extend the registry's merge retention (which already protects `models`) to
  `skills`/`slashCommands`, or seed the pi driver's initial snapshot from the on-disk cache.
  Recommendation: **track it and fix it as its own small change** — it is deterministic,
  frequent, and now well understood, but it touches a different layer and deserves its own review.

  <ReviewChoice itemId="d4" label="D4 — restart window as follow-up" />
</Card>

<Card id="d5" heading="D5 · Enrichment cadence: 2 minutes is self-defeating" tone="warning" badge="STARVATION" meta={["SNAPSHOT_REFRESH_INTERVAL", "~720 pi spawns/day", "one-constant change"]}>
  pi refreshes every 2 minutes where every other driver uses 5 — ~720 throwaway pi processes per
  day, each paying a 3.4–12 s cold boot, regardless of whether anyone is connected. Worse, the
  arithmetic is broken: worst-case enrichment (boot + 90 s models + 90 s commands) exceeds the
  interval, so each tick can interrupt the previous enrichment forever under exactly the load
  conditions the 90 s timeout was raised for. Recommendation: **align to 5 minutes in this change**
  — it is one constant, it restores interval > worst-case, and with D1/D2 in place a slower refresh
  carries no staleness risk to the palette (the last good palette already stands). The interval
  value itself is the one genuinely balanced call — see the question below.

  <ReviewChoice itemId="d5" label="D5 — fix the cadence" />
</Card>

<Card id="d6" heading="D6 · The composer's empty state — defer" tone="neutral" badge="DEFER" meta={["ChatComposer / ComposerCommandMenu", "needs staleness signal"]}>
  "No skills found. Try / to browse provider commands." asserts a failure as fact and recommends a
  menu the same failure empties. Distinguishing "you have no skills" from "the last refresh failed"
  properly needs a staleness/failure marker on the provider snapshot — a contract change reaching
  the client. After D1+D2, false emptiness mostly stops occurring (the palette holds its last good
  value instead), so the copy is stale only for genuinely skill-less users. Recommendation:
  **defer**; revisit only if the D3 warning shows the condition still reaching users.

  <ReviewChoice itemId="d6" label="D6 — defer empty-state rework" />
</Card>
